against preferred direction: router cost of routing a trace perpendicular to a layer's preferred direction
air line: DRC visualization of an incomplete connection between two items
annular ring: the copper pad remaining around a drilled hole
attach smd: a via or trace connection anchored to the center of a surface-mount pad
autoroute: run the automatic router on selected items or the whole board (verb; distinct from the autorouter engine)
autorouter: the batch automatic routing engine that connects nets with traces and vias
bend cost: router penalty added when a trace changes direction on a layer
board outline: the PCB edge boundary; copper and keepouts must stay inside it
clearance: the minimum allowed distance between two copper or mechanical features
clearance class: a named group of spacing rules applied to traces, vias, and areas
clearance matrix: table defining clearance values between item classes on a layer
clearance violation: a design-rule failure where two items are closer than allowed
component: a placed footprint instance on the board
component keepout: a zone where components must not be placed; UI also calls this place keepout
conduction area: a filled copper region tied to one net (copper pour or plane); Freerouting name for that area
copper pour: a filled copper region for a net; KiCad name. Freerouting models this as a conduction area
copper-to-edge clearance: minimum distance from copper to the board outline; not present in typical KiCad DSN exports
courtyard: the minimum keepout boundary around a component body
DRC: design-rule check: verification of clearances, widths, and other manufacturing rules
DSN: Specctra design file (.dsn) exchanged with KiCad, EAGLE, and similar EDA tools
expansion cost: internal maze-routing cost used to rank candidate path expansions
fab: fabrication layer showing component body outlines for assembly drawings
fanout: short traces and vias from dense pads (e.g. BGA) to escape routing layers
footprint: the land pattern of a component on the board; Specctra calls this a package
FRB: Freerouting binary board file (.frb); keep the name FRB
gate: Specctra term for a logical grouping of pins within a component
gate pin: a pin referenced through a component gate in Specctra format
ground plane: a copper pour or plane used for ground distribution
hole: a drilled opening in the board, plated or unplated
incomplete: a connection that still needs routing (one ratsnest air wire)
incompletes: incomplete connections still shown in the ratsnest
jump wire: a discrete wire or single-sided routing layer used instead of a copper trace
keepout: a zone where traces, vias, or placement are forbidden
layer: a PCB copper, mask, silkscreen, or documentation plane
length violation: a net whose routed trace length is outside the allowed minimum or maximum
logical part: Specctra term for a component definition before placement
microvia: a small laser-drilled via that spans only adjacent layers
neckdown: automatic trace width reduction where the route enters a narrower pad
net: an electrical connection grouping all pins that must be connected
net class: a set of routing rules (trace width, via rule, clearance) shared by nets
netlist: the list of nets and pin connections that define electrical connectivity
obstacle area: a copper or mechanical area that blocks or restricts routing
optimizer: post-routing pass that shortens and cleans up existing traces
package: Specctra term for a footprint / land-pattern definition
pad: copper land on a layer where a pin or via connects
padstack: the pad + drill hole pattern defining a pin or via on each layer
pass: one full autorouter iteration over the board; UI also says start pass and maximum passes
pin: a component terminal that must be connected by copper
pin swap: exchange equivalent pins or gates to improve routing
place keepout: zone where components must not be placed; same as component keepout
plated hole: a hole whose wall is metallized so layers are electrically connected
plane via costs: via cost when a net connects to a power or ground plane
power plane: a copper pour layer used for power or ground distribution
preferred direction: horizontal or vertical routing bias configured per signal layer
preferred-direction cost: layer cost of routing a trace in that layer's preferred direction
pull tight: interactive operation that straightens and optimizes trace geometry
push and shove: interactive routing mode that pushes existing traces aside (shove)
ratsnest: temporary air-wire lines showing unrouted connections between pads
reference designator: component identifier printed on silkscreen (for example R1, U3)
rip-up start costs: starting penalty for removing existing traces so they can be rerouted
ripup: remove existing trace segments so a net can be rerouted
rules file: Freerouting design-rules file (.rules) saved separately from the board
score: numeric board quality used to compare routing results (unrouted nets and violations)
SES: Specctra session file (.ses) containing routing results for import
shove: displace an existing trace during interactive routing (the shove action)
shove fixed: net attribute: trace cannot be displaced by push/shove routing
signal layer: a copper layer used for trace routing (not plane-only)
silkscreen: legend layer for reference designators and other markings
SMD: surface-mount device pad (not a through-hole pin)
solder mask: insulating coating layer that leaves pads exposed for soldering
Specctra: PCB interchange format (also called Electra DSN) used by Freerouting
stitch mode: routing mode used for shove-fixed nets that must stay in place
stitching: interactive routing by clicking corners to place the route manually
stitching via: a via placed to tie a copper pour or plane to a net, not to change signal layer
system fixed: item locked by the system so the user cannot move or delete it
teardrop: copper fillet that widens a trace where it meets a pad or via
terminal item: a connectable board item at the end of a route (pin, via, area)
thermal relief: spoke-like copper connection from a pad to a plane, limiting heat flow during soldering
trace: a copper track connecting pads, vias, or areas on one layer (KiCad says track)
trace costs: per-layer expansion-cost modifiers for routing on that layer
trace length: the routed length of a copper trace
trace width: the copper width of a trace, usually from the net class
unfixed: item that is not locked and may be moved, shoved, or deleted
unroute: remove routing from selected items or nets
unrouted: not yet connected by finished copper routing
user fixed: item locked by the user so it cannot be moved or shoved
via: a plated hole connecting traces on different layers
via costs: penalty for placing a layer-change via; higher values keep the router on the current layer
via keepout: a zone where vias are not allowed
via rule: defines which via padstacks and layer spans a net class may use
